seoTitle: How to Verify Your Identity on Stripe and Go Live
metaDescription: Complete Stripe's account activation flow: verify your business, link an existing account, add extras like tax calculation, and switch from test keys to live mode.
intro:
A brand-new Stripe account can generate test API keys and simulate charges immediately, but nothing collected in test mode turns into real money until the account is activated. Stripe calls this verifying your business: it collects identity documents, a home address, and legal-entity information under Know Your Customer rules that apply to every account, not just larger ones.

This guide follows that flow screen by screen, from the dashboard prompt that starts it to the tax-category setting that trips up a lot of first-time sellers, and flags one decision Stripe won't let you undo later.
prerequisites: A government-issued photo ID for identity verification
A document showing your home address
Business registration or legal-entity documents; the exact ones depend on your country and entity type
A bank account to receive payouts once you're live
costNote: Activating an account costs nothing. Stripe's own pricing page states plainly that it doesn't charge setup fees, monthly fees, or closure fees. Once you're live, per-transaction processing fees apply on every charge; those rates vary by country and payment method, so check Stripe's pricing page for your own region instead of assuming a flat number.

steps.heading: Find the activation prompt on your dashboard
steps.body: Your Stripe dashboard Home shows Gross volume, USD balance, and Payouts at a glance, but the piece that matters before you can accept real money is the Recommendations panel and the Setup guide in the corner, listing Verify your business, Complete your profile, and similar unchecked items. Until those are done, the account only processes test transactions. The API keys shown in Recommendations are prefixed pk_test_ and sk_test_ for exactly that reason: live keys don't exist until activation finishes.

image.caption: The Stripe dashboard Home, with the Recommendations panel and Setup guide checklist prompting business verification before test-mode API keys become live ones.

steps.heading: Start Activate your account and link or create a business
steps.body:
Clicking into activation opens a flow with four numbered steps on the left: Verify your business, Add your bank, Add extras, and Review and submit. The first real question is whether to link the account to an existing business already on your Stripe profile, shown as a card with the business name, creation date, and registered address, or start fresh with Create a new business. Linking an existing one carries over tax details, ownership, and management information automatically.

One decision here is permanent: once a service is activated on a live account, Stripe won't let you change the business's origin country. If you're opening this account for a business based in a different country than the one you're about to select, get that right before you submit, not after you've gone live.

image.caption: The Verify your business step, asking whether to link the account to an existing registered business or create a new one.

steps.heading: Complete your business and banking details accurately
steps.body:
Stripe then walks through the identity and business details it needs: legal name, address, and whatever KYC information applies in your country. The most common source of delay is a mismatch. If the name or address you type doesn't exactly match your official documents, Stripe's automated checks can't confirm it, and the review either takes longer or gets kicked to a human. Document-based checks on legal-entity paperwork specifically can take up to 24 hours once submitted.

This section also sets the business name, support contact and statement descriptor your customers see on their card statement or receipt. A vague or unrecognizable descriptor is a common cause of customers disputing a charge as unfamiliar, so pick something customers will recognize. Add your bank comes right after, since that's the account payouts will land in once you're live.

steps.heading: Set your tax category during Add extras
steps.body: The Add extras step includes an optional screen, Automate tax collection on your sales, where Stripe pre-fills a product category based on what it knows about your business. The default often covers only a generic digital item. The screen recommends picking something more specific, software, digital goods, cloud services, website services, if that better matches what you sell, since the category affects how tax is calculated on every future transaction.

image.caption: The Add extras step's tax calculation screen, with a pre-filled product category you can narrow to match what you sell.

steps.heading: Review, submit, then wait for approval
steps.body:
Review and submit is the last chance to catch a typo in an address or a mismatched name before it goes to Stripe for verification. Go through business details, the bank account, and the tax category methodically; resubmitting after a rejection takes longer than getting it right the first time.

Verification times vary by country and account type, from a few minutes to a few business days, and Stripe emails you once it's resolved. Once approved, check the dashboard for the toggle between test and live mode. Real transactions only process in live mode, and running one small real payment yourself confirms money reaches your bank before you send customers to a live checkout.

troubleshooting.problem: Verification review is taking days and money is stuck
troubleshooting.cause: Usually a typo or formatting difference between what you typed and your official documents, or your country requires extra KYC information Stripe hasn't collected yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Check every field against the exact wording on your documents before submitting. If Stripe flags something, it emails specific instructions; respond with corrected documents instead of starting over.

troubleshooting.problem: Need to switch the business's country after going live
troubleshooting.cause: Stripe locks the business origin country the moment a service is activated on a live account.
troubleshooting.fix: There's no edit path for this. If the business is based elsewhere, you need to create a separate Stripe account under the correct country.

troubleshooting.problem: A customer disputes a charge as unrecognized
troubleshooting.cause: The statement descriptor or public business name on their card statement doesn't clearly match your brand.
troubleshooting.fix: Update the statement descriptor and public business details under Account settings so charges are instantly recognizable.

faq.question: What documents does Stripe require for verification?
faq.answer: A government-issued photo ID, a document showing your home address, and legal-entity paperwork appropriate to your country and business type, such as a certificate of incorporation or partnership agreement.

faq.question: How long does Stripe identity verification take?
faq.answer: From a few minutes to a few business days overall. Legal-entity document reviews specifically can take up to 24 hours once submitted.

faq.question: Can I accept real payments before verification finishes?
faq.answer: No. You can build and test your integration with the pk_test_/sk_test_ keys, but real charges require an activated account in live mode.

faq.question: Can I change my business's country after I go live?
faq.answer: No. Stripe locks the business origin country once you've activated a service on a live account. Getting this right during Verify your business matters, since there's no edit path afterward.

faq.question: Do I need to set a tax category during activation?
faq.answer: It's optional. Stripe pre-fills a general category during Add extras, but narrowing it to match what you sell improves how accurately tax is calculated.
